title: Learning trombone with William Moore at the power plant
summary: Studying applied electricity, he works summer shifts at the power plant with clarinetist William Moore, who drills him on music, and Captain Dryer rewards him with a new Conn trombone.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

a clarinet player, a very fine musician and by me working up my way and everything, I was staying--I wasn't coming home then, so I was going to work all that summer

Applied electricity. I wanted to be in the band but no music was connected as my livelihood.

Yeah, that's it. So he says, I tell you what, he was on the second band, if you could get assigned to work with me this summer at the power plant, we would change dynamos, work so many hours and then we cleaned it off and this and that, and changed the dynamo over for the next twenty four hours, and he said if you work with me down there, what we will do is drill. He said I'll drill you three or four hours every morning and before we go to bed.
So I talked to the electrical instructor and told him I wasn't going home and

would he assign me with Moore--William Moore-- and so he told me yes he would, and so Moore and I would come in and he would take his clarinet, because he could transpose, and work along with me and everything. He would tell me I'm coming along and I would practice and so when school started I was in the band--they put me in the band, and I still had this horn that he had repaired.
The Captain had his eye on me and so along about the middle of that school term he says I got a surprise for you, and so he called me up to his office and had a brand new Conn.
He moved me up to second bone and he said I knew that all you needed was something to play.
